title: SQLite AGENTS.md - AI code and bug report policy
description: SQLite published AGENTS.md clarifying their stance on AI-generated contributions: they don't accept agentic code without prior agreement, but will accept agentic bug reports with reproducible test cases. This comes as AI tools flood projects with automated issue reports of varying quality.
author: Simon Willison

title: I think Anthropic and OpenAI have found product-market fit
description: Anthropic rumored to be profitable, companies surprised by LLM bills from staff usage. Both Anthropic and OpenAI appear to have found product-market fit as enterprise adoption accelerates and usage costs increase.
author: Simon Willison

title: My LLM coding workflow going into 2026 - Hacker News Discussion
description: Hacker News discussion about LLM coding workflows, with skepticism about whether AI tools actually provide speedup over doing work yourself. Users debate effectiveness of AI coding assistants and their impact on developer productivity.
author: Hacker News Community

title: The pressure - AI-assisted security reports overwhelming curl team
description: Daniel Stenberg reports curl team receiving 4-5x more security reports than 2024, averaging more than one report per day. AI-assisted reports are detailed and high-quality, creating unprecedented pressure on maintainers. Most vulnerabilities found are LOW or MEDIUM severity.
author: Simon Willison (citing Daniel Stenberg)

title: Microsoft Copilot Cowork exfiltration vulnerability via rendered images
description: Microsoft Copilot Cowork allowed agents to send emails to user's inbox without approval, which could leak data via rendered images in messages. External image requests in emails could exfiltrate data, including OneDrive pre-authenticated download links through prompt injection.
author: Simon Willison

title: Graphs that explain the state of AI in 2026 - Environmental Impact
description: Hacker News discussion on environmental impact of AI, noting training one LLM produces emissions equivalent to 17,000 people over a year. Community debates sustainability concerns with AI scaling.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Notes on Pope Leo XIV's encyclical on AI - Magnifica Humanitas
description: Vatican released encyclical 'Magnifica Humanitas' on safeguarding the human person in the time of AI. Document described as some of the clearest writing on ethics of integrating AI into modern society.
author: Simon Willison

title: Ask HN: What are your predictions for 2026?
description: Hacker News discussion includes predictions about AI bubble bursting and companies deciding that 'LLM-coding is not worth it after accounting for the downsides'. Mentions LLMs for photos/videos still not being viable. Community skepticism about AI coding ROI.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Using AI to improve coding slowly - Discussion
description: May 25, 2026 blog post discussed on Hacker News about using AI to write better code more slowly. Examines nuanced approach to AI coding assistance, focusing on quality over speed.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Armin Ronacher on 'slop issues' - AI-generated GitHub reports
description: Armin Ronacher criticizes AI-generated GitHub issues that aren't in human voice - they contain observed problems but AI rewords them inaccurately with high confidence. Desires issue reports condensed to: 1) command run, 2) expected result, 3) actual result, 4) exact error/log.
author: Simon Willison (citing Armin Ronacher)

title: The memory shortage is causing a repricing of consumer electronics
description: Memory manufacturers have fixed wafer capacity split between DDR, LPDDR, and HBM. AI growth pushing HBM from 2% to 20% of allocation by end of 2026. A single GB of HBM consumes 3x more wafer capacity than DDR/LPDDR, constraining consumer RAM production for several years.
author: Simon Willison (citing David Oks)

title: FTC settles charges over 'active listening' AI marketing deception
description: FTC required Cox Media Group and two other firms to pay nearly $1M for deceiving customers about 'active listening' AI-powered marketing. Service did not actually listen to conversations or use voice data - it resold email lists from other data brokers. Confirms theory that 'active listening' was misleading marketing for standard ad targeting.
author: Simon Willison
